newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-PSV GAME SWITCHED TO CONTROL FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-PSV GAME SWITCHED TO CONTROL FANS.

text.p: Sunday's Dutch first division soccer match between Feyenoord Rotterdam and PSV Eindhoven has been brought forward to 2.30pm (1330 GMT) from the scheduled evening kick-off.
Rotterdam mayor Bram Peper said he wanted the game brought forward so that police could more easily control supporters during daylight hours, a spokesman for the mayor said.
"He wanted the match played in daylight. We also believed fans from PSV would travel to the city centre before the match," the spokesman said.
The last two years, small groups of PSV fans have caused disturbances in the city centre before games.
Police expect up to 50,000 fans to attend the game, seen as the Dutch league title decider.
As mayor, Peper is chief of the Rotterdam police and can introduce special decrees if he thinks public order may be disrupted.

The Dutch football association (KNVB) had planned to televise the game live, but will not do so on Sunday afternoon. They said they were unhappy with the Rotterdam authorities who, they say, had authorised the origninal schedule before the start of the season.
Rotterdam's Feyenoord stadium is due to host to the European Cup Winners' Cup and Dutch Cup finals in May and the Netherlands-Belgium clash in the autumn.
